title: 5 EASY Latin DANCE STEPS You NEED [STEP BY STEP] Beginners

method.teacher_system: The teacher begins by establishing the importance of posture and weight distribution. She then breaks down five distinct dance steps, demonstrating each one clearly before adding layers of body movement to increase the difficulty. Finally, she guides the learner through a practice routine to consolidate the steps.
method.signature: The teacher consistently offers a 'Level Up' version for every basic step, allowing learners to add styling and body movement at their own pace.

practices.what: The teacher breaks down the first step, focusing on heel movement and weight transfer.
The teacher adds hip and chest movements to the first step to increase the difficulty.
The teacher introduces the second step, focusing on side-to-side movement.
The teacher adds shoulder movements to the second step.
The teacher breaks down the third step, which involves three side steps.
The teacher adds hip, torso, and arm movements to the third step.
The teacher introduces the fourth step, focusing on forward and backward movement.
The teacher adds hip movement to the fourth step.
The teacher breaks down the fifth step, which involves opening to the back.
The teacher adds body movement and heel touches to the fifth step.
The teacher leads a full practice routine of all five steps with music.

adaptations.difficulty: Stretching the knees too much blocks body movement.
adaptations.adjustment: Keep the knees and butt relaxed.

adaptations.difficulty: Basic step might feel too simple.
adaptations.adjustment: Add hip and chest movement to level up.
Move the arms with the torso.
Cross the leg slightly to the back.

beliefs.belief: The teacher believes that knowing how to shift weight and bend knees is the first essential thing to dance Latin rhythm.

moments.says: The teacher invites the learner to get started with learning easy Latin dance steps.
The teacher explains the foundational posture of weight forward and bent knees, warning against stretching legs which blocks movement.
The teacher suggests adding upper body movements to take the first dance step to the next level.
The teacher demonstrates how to add hip, torso, and arm movements while reminding the learner how arms should not look.
The teacher encourages the learner to practice all the learned steps together from the top.

mentor.what_stays: The teacher leaves the learner feeling equipped and excited to show off new dance moves at any party.

method.limits: The video does not show partner work or specific gender-based styling nuances, which were requested by learners.
